text:
matan: Hi all 44b first-day question. I ran the repo quickstart but my locally-run Python backend can't talk to the Postgres container. Error: `psycopg2.OperationalError: could not connect to server: Connection refused\n\tIs the server running on host "127.0.0.1" and accepting TCP/IP connections on port 5432?`

matan: I inspected containers: `docker ps` shows postgres:latest up. `docker logs` says database system is ready to accept connections.

devex: welcome! Quick checklist: 1) Are you running the app on your host or inside a container? 2) Does your compose map host ports to the container? Share the pg service snippet.

matan: I'm running the app on host (fast reloads). Compose snippet from repo: ```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:14
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432"
```

sophia: subtle: `ports: - "5432"` publishes the port but doesn't necessarily bind it to 0.0.0.0 on the host in all setups. For host access use `"5432:5432"`.

matan: changed to `5432:5432`, recreated containers, `docker ps` now shows `0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp` but `psql -h localhost -U postgres` still fails with connection refused.

devex: three possibilities: 1) a local Postgres is already bound to 5432 (check `lsof -i:5432`), 2) bind-mount permission prevented PG from actually starting even if logs later said ready, 3) if you're on WSL2 Docker Desktop the mapping can be on the VM network, not the WSL host localhost. Which OS are you on?

matan: using Docker Desktop for Windows (WSL2 backend). `lsof` shows nothing. `docker logs` earlier did have `could not open lock file "postmaster.pid": Permission denied` before I chowned the folder, then it printed ready.

sophia: permission errors are common with host bind mounts. Named volumes avoid that: `volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and top-level `volumes:\n  pgdata:`. If you need host files, chown to uid 999/gid 999 or run an init container to fix ownership.

matan: switched to named volume and recreated. Postgres inside container is reachable from other containers, e.g. `docker run --rm --network myproj_default --rm appropriate/curl nc -vz db 5432` succeeds. Host still can't connect to localhost:5432 though.

devex: that strongly suggests the host<->container binding isn't exposed to your environment (WSL2/network boundary). On Docker Desktop/WSL2 use `host.docker.internal` from the host to reach the Docker VM, but WSL behavior is inconsistent. Try `psql -h host.docker.internal -p 5432 -U postgres`.

matan: `host.docker.internal` didn't resolve from my WSL shell initially. I ran `docker run --rm --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway busybox nslookup host.docker.internal` and it worked inside containers but not from WSL host.

sophia: in WSL you can add `extra_hosts: - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"` to the postgres service so the container knows the host alias, but that helps container->host, not host->container. For host->container on WSL sometimes the safest is mapping to a different host port like `"5433:5432"` and connect to localhost:5433 from WSL. Alternatively run your app in a dev container that mounts your source and exposes app port so it lives on the same compose network and can use `db:5432` directly.

matan: I tried mapping `5433:5432` and now `psql -h localhost -p 5433` from WSL connects! Nice workaround.

devex: great. Also note Windows users on Docker Desktop M1/mac can run into mac-specific socket/permission issues; on macOS, `host.docker.internal` usually works out of the box, on Linux it's `host-gateway` via extra_hosts. For dev ergonomics we recommend two patterns: 1) run the app in a dev container (source mounted) so service DNS works, or 2) use a `dev-host` compose profile that maps common ports (`5432:5432`, `6379:6379`) and uses named volumes.

msys-bot: (sys-bot) postgres:14 image pulled and volume pgdata created :white_check_mark:

matan: one more: redis was failing earlier when I ran my app on host because REDIS_URL was set to `redis://redis:6379` in .env (service name). switched to `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379` after mapping `6379:6379` and fixed it.

sophia: yea that's another frequent trap: service hostnames only resolve between containers. If you ever see `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND redis` or similar from a host process, that's likely the issue.

matan: thanks all, learned a lot. I'll open a tiny README PR suggesting: (a) prefer named volumes for PG in dev, (b) explain `"ports: \"5432\"` vs `"5432:5432"`, (c) note WSL/host.docker.internal quirks and the `5433` workaround, and (d) recommend running dev server in a container for consistent DNS. cc @devex for review. :tada:
